title: Validate logical Arrow coordinates before serializing physical values
applies_when: A public numeric query is serialized from an Arrow array whose coordinates must all be present, but implementation code iterates raw value buffers.
lesson: Arrow validity is separate from physical values. Trace the real public query through serialization, vary finite bytes beneath the same null slot, and retain all-valid and sliced-null-outside controls. Reject a required coordinate's null before reading its physical value; this is distinct from non-finite-number validation. Identical logical data must not produce different requests solely because hidden null-slot bytes differ.
avoid_when: Do not reject every explicit validity bitmap: an all-valid array may have one, and a null outside the logical slice is irrelevant. Nullable-coordinate APIs may intentionally define another contract. Remote-query evidence does not qualify local-query semantics, rebuilt bindings, live Cloud, throughput or maintainer acceptance.

evidence.note: Validity is separate from physical value storage; a zero null count may still have an explicit all-valid bitmap. This is a format contract, not application qualification.

Native remote-table/public-query regression: identical logical [0.1, null] with backing values 0 or 123 sends different numeric requests on unchanged main (four failures). The remote-only null guard passes 10 focused cases and 277 remote table tests, including all-valid and sliced controls. HTTP is mocked; live Cloud, rebuilt bindings, local-query semantics and performance are unqualified. Fork publication is not maintainer acceptance.
